Title: Invoice paid in part, then in full
Description: Create and post an invoice, apply a partial payment and check the balance, then apply the remainder.
Expected Result: The balance falls after each payment, and the invoice shows as paid in the customer account and the receipts register.

Title: Credit note against an invoice
Description: Issue a credit note for part of a posted invoice and apply it.
Expected Result: The invoice balance falls by the credit, and the revenue and tax postings reverse in proportion.

Title: Tax and rounding on a multi-line invoice
Description: Enter an invoice with many small lines, a mix of taxable and exempt items, and a discount. Compare line-level and invoice-level tax.
Expected Result: Tax follows the documented rounding rule, and the total equals the sum of its parts to the cent.

Title: Pricing: discounts and markups
Description: Apply a percentage discount, then a fixed discount, then a customer price list or markup, to an invoice.
Expected Result: Each adjustment calculates correctly on its own and in combination, and the invoice shows what was applied.

Title: Recurring invoice run
Description: Set up a recurring invoice (monthly, with one price change), run it for three periods, and review the results.
Expected Result: One invoice is created per period, with the right dates and amounts, and a rerun creates no duplicates.

Title: Customer statement and aging agree with open invoices
Description: Run the customer statement and the aging report, and compare them with the list of open invoices.
Expected Result: Both show the same open items, and every item sits in the right aging bucket.

Title: Duplicate invoice number is refused
Description: Enter a second invoice with the number of one already posted.
Expected Result: The system refuses it or warns clearly, and no duplicate is posted.

Title: Milestone or progress billing
Description: Bill a contract in stages: a deposit, a percentage of completion, and a final invoice.
Expected Result: Amounts billed to date never exceed the contract value, and each stage is posted to the right period.

Title: Invoice delivery by email
Description: Email two invoices, one to a separate billing contact, and check the invoice register.
Expected Result: The right address receives each invoice, and the register shows both as sent.

Title: Overpayment and unapplied cash
Description: Receive a payment larger than the invoice, then one with no invoice to match.
Expected Result: The excess is held as unapplied credit, can be applied later, and the customer balance is correct.

Title: Bad debt write-off
Description: Write off an uncollectable invoice, then receive a late payment for it.
Expected Result: The write-off posts to the expense account, and the late payment reverses it correctly.

Title: Foreign currency invoice paid at a different rate
Description: Issue an invoice in a foreign currency and receive payment after the exchange rate has changed.
Expected Result: The exchange gain or loss is posted, and the customer balance clears to zero in both currencies.

Title: Three-way match mismatch is flagged
Description: Receive part of an order, then enter a bill for a different quantity or price.
Expected Result: The mismatch is flagged before payment, and the approver sees the difference.

Title: Bill batch with and without an order, including a split allocation
Description: Enter a batch of bills: some matched to an order, some not, and one split across several accounts.
Expected Result: Each bill posts with the right allocation, and the batch review lists them correctly.

Title: Payment run selected by due date and supplier
Description: Build a payment run by due date, for one supplier and for all suppliers, and select bills from several suppliers.
Expected Result: Totals follow the selection, and only bills that are due and approved are offered.

Title: Print, cancel and reinstate a payment
Description: Print payments for a set of bills, cancel one, and reinstate it.
Expected Result: The payment register is correct after each step, the bill reopens on cancel, and the audit shows both actions.

Title: Duplicate payment is prevented
Description: Select the same bill twice in one payment, then try to pay a bill that was already paid.
Expected Result: A clear warning blocks both, and each bill is paid once.

Title: Create purchase orders with each line type
Description: Create orders with a stocked item, a non-stocked item, a service, and a comment line.
Expected Result: All lines save correctly, and the order total is right.

Title: Receive an order in full and in part
Description: Receive one order fully and another partially.
Expected Result: Quantities received and outstanding are right, and the order status follows.

Title: Revise, cancel and close an order
Description: Revise a released order, cancel another, and close a third with a quantity still open.
Expected Result: The revision history is kept, cancelled orders cannot be received, and closing releases the open commitment.

Title: Correct the number of a posted bill
Description: Change the reference number of a posted bill and add a note.
Expected Result: The new number shows everywhere, the note is kept, and the audit log records who changed it.

Title: Early payment discount and late fee
Description: Pay one bill inside its discount window and another after its due date.
Expected Result: The discount or fee is calculated by the terms on the bill and posted to the right accounts.

Title: Post a balanced ledger entry
Description: Post a balanced entry with a note attached and look it up in the ledger inquiry.
Expected Result: The entry appears with the right accounts, amounts, period and note.

Title: Reject an unbalanced ledger entry
Description: Try to post an entry where debits and credits differ by one cent.
Expected Result: The entry is refused with a clear message and nothing is posted.

Title: Trial balance agrees with the account and history inquiries
Description: Run the account inquiry and the history inquiry for one period and compare them with the trial balance.
Expected Result: Balances in all three agree for every account checked.

Title: Posting into a closed period is refused
Description: Try to post an entry dated in a closed period.
Expected Result: The posting is refused, or needs an authorised override that is recorded in the audit log.

Title: Close and reopen a period
Description: Close a period, confirm postings are blocked, reopen it with authority, post a correction, and close it again.
Expected Result: Closing blocks postings, reopening is logged, and the correction lands in the right period.

Title: Bank reconciliation
Description: Import a bank statement, match it with ledger entries, and leave a few items unmatched.
Expected Result: Matched items clear, unmatched items stay listed, and the reconciled balance equals the statement balance.

Title: Financial statements balance
Description: Produce the balance sheet and income statement for a period, and compare them with the trial balance.
Expected Result: Assets equal liabilities plus equity, and net income ties to the retained earnings movement.

Title: Sub-ledgers reconcile to the ledger
Description: Run receivables aging, payables aging and the inventory valuation, and compare each with its control account at the period end date.
Expected Result: Each sub-ledger total equals its control account.

Title: Recurring and reversing ledger entries
Description: Create a monthly recurring entry and an accrual that reverses on the first day of the next period.
Expected Result: Each entry posts in the right period, and the reversal cancels the original exactly.

Title: Currency revaluation at period end
Description: Hold foreign currency balances at period end and run the revaluation.
Expected Result: Unrealised gains and losses post once, with a reversal on the first day of the next period.

Title: Stock valuation agrees with the ledger
Description: Run the valuation report and the transaction log, then compare their totals with the inventory account.
Expected Result: The valuation, the log and the account agree in total.

Title: Costing method changes cost correctly
Description: Receive the same item at three different prices, then sell part of it under average cost, then under first-in first-out.
Expected Result: Cost of sales and remaining stock value follow each method exactly.

Title: Stock count cycle
Description: Take a count snapshot, enter counts for each location, and post the differences.
Expected Result: Counts are recorded against the snapshot, and the variance posts once to stock and the ledger.

Title: Receipts and adjustments change quantity on hand
Description: Receive stock, then make a positive and a negative adjustment.
Expected Result: Quantity and value move by the expected amounts, and stock cannot go below zero unless the setting allows it.

Title: Counter sale and return
Description: Sell items over the counter, reverse one sale, and return part of another.
Expected Result: Stock, sales and tax update on sale and return to their starting values on reversal.

Title: Acquire an asset and run depreciation
Description: Add an asset with a cost, useful life and method, and run depreciation for three periods.
Expected Result: Depreciation posts each period by the chosen method, and the book value falls by the same amounts.

Title: Dispose of an asset
Description: Sell an asset part-way through its life and record the proceeds.
Expected Result: The gain or loss is posted, depreciation stops, and the asset leaves the register.

Title: Gross to net calculation
Description: Enter hours for four employees, including overtime, and calculate taxes and deductions.
Expected Result: Net pay equals gross pay less deductions for each employee, with no rounding drift.

Title: Pay register agrees with the ledger after the update
Description: Print the pay register, compare it with the pay record inquiry, then run the payroll update and check the ledger.
Expected Result: The register, the records and the ledger postings show the same figures.

Title: Payment output for each pay method
Description: Print cheques, create the direct deposit file and email the earnings statements.
Expected Result: Amounts, names and bank details are correct on every output.

Title: Employee and pay period setup
Description: Create a pay period and two employees, one paid by cheque and one by direct deposit with an emailed earnings statement.
Expected Result: Both employees save with the right payment method and bank or email details.

Title: Tax rate change takes effect on the right date
Description: Add a new tax rate with a future start date, then enter invoices dated before and after it.
Expected Result: Invoices before the date use the old rate, and invoices on or after it use the new one.

Title: Tax return totals agree with the ledger
Description: Run the tax return for a period and compare each box with the ledger tax accounts.
Expected Result: Tax collected, tax paid and the balance due agree with the ledger.

Title: Role-based access
Description: Sign in as a user without permission and try to view, post, approve and export in each area.
Expected Result: Each action is limited as configured, and refused actions are logged.

Title: Creator cannot approve their own transaction
Description: Create a bill, a payment and a ledger entry, then try to approve each with the same user.
Expected Result: Self-approval is blocked, and a second user can approve.

Title: Approval limits route to the right approver
Description: Submit transactions just below, at and just above an approval limit.
Expected Result: Each goes to the approver for its amount, and none skips a level.

Title: Audit trail records every change
Description: Edit, delete and reverse records in several areas, then read the audit log.
Expected Result: Each entry shows who, when, what changed, and the values before and after.

Title: Attach supporting documents to a record
Description: Attach an image and a PDF at the same time to a customer, supplier or transaction, then find them by date and filter.
Expected Result: Both files are saved and can be opened from the record and from the document list.

Title: Invoice PDF includes chosen attachments
Description: Choose attachments to merge into an invoice, produce the PDF, and open it.
Expected Result: The PDF contains the invoice followed by the chosen documents in order.

Title: Export and import round trip
Description: Export invoices to CSV and import the file into an empty test company.
Expected Result: Totals, taxes and customer links match, and bad rows are reported rather than skipped silently.
